name: Most stringent bound on electron neutrino mass obtained with a scalable low temperature microcalorimeter array

significance.quote: With a total of 7 × 107 decay events recorded over two months and a Bayesian statistical analysis, we derive an upper limit of mβ < 27 eV/c2 at 90% credibility.

summary.plain: HOLMES watched holmium-163 decays in an array of ultra-cold detectors for two months and found no neutrino mass signal: the electron neutrino weighs less than 27 electron-volts at 90% credibility. The paper called it the most stringent bound from this calorimetric method; ECHo later reported a lower limit.
summary.technical: Two physics runs (about 2 months, about 7×10⁷ events, 48 active TES pixels, 6 eV FWHM): Bayesian limit m_β < 27 eV/c² (90% credibility). The paper states this is the most stringent bound ever obtained with a calorimetric 163Ho measurement (March 2025); ECHo-1k (arXiv:2509.03423) later reported m < 15 eV/c² (90%).

title: Most stringent bound on electron neutrino mass obtained with a scalable low temperature microcalorimeter array
why_it_matters: Shows that ion-implanted TES arrays can scale to a competitive calorimetric neutrino-mass experiment, an independent route to KATRIN's tritium measurements.
